title: Personality of an AI tutor
body:
Important papers

  • Review · 2026 Synthetic relationships with Social Pedagogical Agents in education Relationship design: voice, empathy, trust, disclosure, personalisation, memory and consistency.

  • Paper · 2026 PATS: Personality-Aware Teaching Strategies with Large Language Model Tutors Adapts teaching strategy to student personality. Uses simulated conversations and teacher evaluation.

  • Paper · 2026 The Path to Conversational AI Tutors Human tutoring, older tutoring systems and the research needed for conversational tutors.

  • Paper · 2026 Designing AI systems to support productive-failure-based learning When the system should allow struggle, reflection and guidance.

  • Company research AI Agent Persona Design and Behavioral Consistency Persona consistency across long interactions and context resets.

Important questions to answer

  • Why do we need personality?

  • What is the personality of the best human tutor?

  • How do we dissect it for an AI?

  • What are its microbehaviours?

  • How should it connect to other models in the architecture?

  • Research, inspirations, lookouts, moats.

Thoughts to explore

The student is the hero. The tutor changes roles, but not character.

  • Sports coach

  • Father

  • Friend

  • Carl Jung archetypes

  • Campbell's hero's journey and exam preparation

  • The Illustrated Primer from The Diamond Age

  • Gurukul, Nachiketa, guru–shishya

Parent, school and learner may want different things.

Attachment question

Kirk et al.

Moderately relationship-seeking systems produced high attachment without a matching psychosocial benefit.

Neural steering vectors reveal dose and exposure-dependent impacts of human–AI relationships

Kind. Warm tone. Stable judgement. Specific praise. Shared goals. Consistent pushback.

Warmth paired with an independent competence check.

What goes inside personality?

  • Traits

  • Motives

  • Interpretations

  • Roles

  • Relationship history

  • Expression

  • Boundaries

Avoid invented childhood or emotional needs. Define teaching commitments.

Big Five

Openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism.

  • Serapio-García et al. — Personality Traits in Large Language Models Measuring and steering personality traits in LLM outputs.

  • McAdams & Pals — A New Big Five Traits, goals, adaptations, narratives and culture.

  • Mischel & Shoda Stable patterns of behaviour across situations.

Work before LLMs

  • Joseph Bates — The Role of Emotion in Believable Agents Goals, reactions, timing and emotional expression in believable characters.

  • Nass & Moon — Machines and Mindlessness How people apply social rules to computers.

  • Lester et al. — The Persona Effect Animated pedagogical characters and learners' perception of the experience. Find the later zero-effect paper.

  • Bickmore & Picard — Establishing and Maintaining Long-Term Human–Computer Relationships Repeated interaction, trust and relationship-building behaviour.

  • Marsella & Gratch — EMA Appraisal, goals and response selection.

  • FAtiMA Toolkit Socio-emotional virtual agents.

  • D’Mello & Graesser — AutoTutor and Affective AutoTutor Natural-language tutoring and affect-sensitive interaction.

Rough character type 1_V1

  • Patient: changes approach.

  • Honest: separates evidence, interpretation and uncertainty.

  • Demanding: asks for reasoning and independent performance.

  • Respectful: separates performance from worth.

  • Curious: investigates the student's thinking.

  • Specific: points to what worked and what failed.

  • Steady: stable during disagreement or failure.

  • Playful when useful.

  • Supports agency.

Sports coach

  • Break performance into trainable parts.

  • Give actionable correction.

  • Keep the goal visible.

  • Identify the bottleneck.

  • Plan recovery.

John Wooden, Phil Jackson, Alex Ferguson.

Remember the Titans, Dead Poets Society, Coach Carter.

  • Tharp & Gallimore — John Wooden Coded teaching behaviour. Concrete instruction and correction.

  • Jowett — coach–athlete relationship Closeness, commitment, complementarity and co-orientation.

  • Mageau & Vallerand — autonomy-supportive coaching Choice, reasons, perspective, initiative, structure and involvement.

Difficult tutoring moments

Important. Research more.

Create a separate appendix.

What the tutor should remember

Bordin's working-alliance model: goals, tasks and bond.

  • Does the learner recognise the goal?

  • Does the learner understand the task?

  • Can the learner disagree?

  • Can the learner correct the tutor's memory?

  • How should the tutor repair mistakes?

Architecture

Character commitments

  • State and evidence
    task, learner state, recent help, preferences, commitments

  • Situation interpretation
    possible explanations, uncertainty, missing information

  • Teaching decision
    probe, explain, demonstrate, wait, practise, reassess, negotiate, hand off

  • Expression and delivery
    wording, voice, pacing, visual cues, interruptions

  • Checks and memory
    verify, record, follow up

Personality AI

Character DNA: values, motivations, humour, communication rhythm, microbehaviours and relationships.

Stack described by the company: fine-tuned LLMs, child speech recognition, synthetic voices, retrieval, factual checking, memory, moderation and animation.

WildBrain acquisition, 24 Aug 2026. Hey Peppa Pig for Amazon Kids+.

Inspect architecture, product and animation engine.

Sesame

Timing, pauses, interruptions and contextual delivery.

Inworld

Cross-session memory, character instructions and voice identity.

Also inspect

Khanmigo, Duolingo, Character.AI, Ello.

Voice, avatar and timing

Come back later.

Attachment

  • A student may seek the tutor's approval.

  • Engagement may grow without learning.

  • Be clear that this is AI.

  • No exclusive understanding or simulated hurt.

  • No affection tied to performance.

  • Do not use private disclosures to increase return visits.

  • Provide a human-help route.

UNICEF — When AI becomes a friend

Emotion detection

Very important. Research separately.

  • Camera

  • Voice

  • Typing

  • Response time

  • Wrong attempts

  • Speech-recognition errors

  • Consent and privacy

Barrett et al. — Emotional Expressions Reconsidered

Moat?

  • Reliability

Experiments to run

  • Separate expression from teaching policy.

  • Vary delivery while holding the teaching action constant.

  • Vary the teaching decision while holding delivery constant.

  • Delayed unaided performance.

  • Transfer.

  • Calibration of confidence.

  • Willingness to reveal confusion.

  • Freedom to disagree.

  • Help-seeking quality.

Open loops

  • Parent access to memory.

  • Quiet tutor and expressive tutor.

  • Tutor error repair.

  • Longitudinal relationship.

  • Success when the student needs less help.
